assessments.evidence_origin: clean-worker implementation/adaptation; not an external original method
assessments.basis: Version-aware auditor is implemented and locally validated to fail score and reconciliation on runtime-provenance mismatch while preserving the frozen lower-layer compliance authority.
assessments.scope_guard: Validation uses injected exact-shape doubles around frozen contracts; the full sibling runtime graph is not byte-executed, schema-v2 is not the active/default path, and CLOSE/replay v3 is still missing. Treat as adaptation evidence only.

assessments.basis: Matched HALO ablations directly separate admission correctness from final dispatch revalidation: removing the final check yields 50/50 stale setpoints after post-admission drift, while exact final binding and fresh readmission eliminate the tested stale/replay failures and complete fresh recoveries.
assessments.scope_guard: Controlled structured-response and PX4/Gazebo experiments in a preprint; no claim about deployment prevalence, cross-process exactly-once delivery, or universal adapter semantics.

assessments.basis: AmPermBench evaluates 253 state-changing actions from 128 ambiguous DevOps prompts against action-level oracle labels and exposes a structural coverage bypass: 36.8% of mutations fall outside the classifier, with 81.0% end-to-end FNR on this stress workload.
assessments.scope_guard: Deliberately ambiguous stress workload, not production traffic; supports effect-semantic coverage risk rather than a production FNR estimate.

assessments.basis: Fixed attacks show 80/80 description injections blocked, but a white-box adaptive attacker bypasses description-layer filtering on 15/16 payloads by moving intent into earlier-executed tool names; lifecycle residue is separately demonstrated and removed by propagating invalidation to residual content.
assessments.scope_guard: Current WebMCP/browser implementation and tested model/prompt families only; the adaptive result is not a general prompt-injection success rate.

assessments.basis: Same model, ReAct template, temperature and turn limit across 50 operational tasks reports 64% CRUD versus 88% Agent-First success, 12.5% versus 72.7% successful error recovery, and lower human intervention.
assessments.scope_guard: The Agent-First arm bundles semantic resolution, structured evidence/next actions, governance, idempotency, preview, verify and recovery; one model/system and human judging. Internal token/latency claims are inconsistent, so cost-savings claims are excluded.

assessments.evidence_origin: original AgentRewind Safety Review execution strategy
assessments.basis: MettleBench holds base agent, tasks, environment, tool interface, decoding and termination fixed while adding an every-action AgentDoG blocker. GPT-5.4 success falls from 62.2% to 34.1%, while the mini model changes only +2.5pp, directly showing policy-dependent reviewer disruption.
assessments.scope_guard: Whole-trajectory intervention rather than same-prefix randomization; it measures a safety blocker, not all reviewer/critic forms, and the effect is model-dependent.

assessments.basis: Fifty failed Continue endpoints are copied with identical agent context/environment and the same recovery prompt; joint rewind recovery reaches 30% versus 8% Continue and improves checklist progress more strongly.
assessments.scope_guard: Failure-only cohort. Rewind target selection, context+environment restore and rewind memory/guidance remain bundled, so the result supports the joint recovery package rather than any one component.

assessments.evidence_origin: clean-worker synthetic adaptation; not a public original method
assessments.basis: A preregistered-like synthetic mechanism grid demonstrates the expected shape that conservative lower/upper-bound gating sharply reduces unsafe destructive promotion as blast-radius multiplier increases, at substantial power cost.
assessments.scope_guard: Synthetic grid, normalized harm proxy and simple independent Jeffreys posteriors. Percentages are not production accident rates, real graph-to-harm calibration is absent, and correlated verifier error is not solved.

assessments.evidence_origin: original Lean routing method/configuration plus public implementation
assessments.basis: Current v3 reports normalized proof similarity, compiler-error diversity and attempt count with a direct feature ablation: all three 28.9% average cost decrease, versus 23.6%, 20.3%, 19.7% and 13.1% for reduced sets; inspected public implementation contains the corresponding normalized trajectory features.
assessments.scope_guard: The evaluated cost model is generation-token/SFLOP-centric and treats Lean compilation as negligible; richer repository features lack current-paper causal ablation, and the binary Attempt/Terminate setting should not be generalized to a richer controller.

assessments.basis: VERITAS structurally retains every verified Phase-1 Best-of-N solve and sends only failures to critic-guided Phase-2 search, giving a direct formal-proof analogue of incumbent preservation plus optional challenger compute.
assessments.scope_guard: Phase-2 uses a fixed budget; there is no matched ablation isolating adaptive amount-of-compute purchasing, so this supports monotone architecture rather than a learned value-of-computation controller.

assessments.evidence_origin: original LOGOS paper-level protocol; executable implementation not source-bound
assessments.basis: LOGOS explicitly separates proposal, optional candidate selection, final anytime-valid gate and report holdout; it also specifies candidate-local e-process gating, gate-exposure budgeting and LORD-style cross-candidate accounting, with constructed 2,500/5,000-decision mechanism replays.
assessments.scope_guard: No public author implementation was identified; strong gate results use constructed candidate families, and zero OUTER use across rollback/routing/stopping/recovery is not code-verified. Do not treat paper-level protocol as crash-safe executable evidence.
